claim.quote: The effects of oscillations of atmospheric νµ are observed in the 5.90 fiducial kiloton-year exposure of the Soudan 2 detector.

date.note: arXiv v1 date; published Phys. Rev. D 68, 113004 (2003) per the DOI on the arXiv record.

key_value_text.quote: The probability of the no oscillation hypothesis is 5.8x10-4
key_value_text.value: Probability of the no-oscillation hypothesis 5.8e-4 in 5.90 fiducial kt-yr; allowed region in the sin^2(2 theta), delta m^2 plane at 90 % confidence

name: Observation of Atmospheric Neutrino Oscillations in Soudan 2

significance.quote: The probability of the no oscillation hypothesis is 5.8x10-4
significance.value: probability of the no-oscillation hypothesis 5.8 x 10^-4

summary.plain: Using its whole data set, Soudan 2 saw the signature of atmospheric muon neutrinos oscillating, in the way their energy and travel distance fit together. The chance of no oscillation was about 6 in 10,000, consistent with Super-Kamiokande's result.
summary.technical: Unbinned maximum-likelihood analysis of the neutrino L/E distribution (Feldman-Cousins) of the 5.90 fiducial kt-yr exposure: probability of no oscillation 5.8e-4; 90 % CL allowed region consistent with Super-Kamiokande.

title: Observation of Atmospheric Neutrino Oscillations in Soudan 2
why_it_matters: A second, independent detector technology (a tracking calorimeter rather than water Cherenkov) seeing atmospheric-neutrino oscillations.
